verdict.rationale: Slate documents a permission system in slate.json. Each permission key maps to "allow", "ask", or "deny", or to a pattern object for fine-grained control, so a lead can govern what the agent may do. The evidence never lists which tools or external integrations those keys cover, so control over external integrations specifically is only implied. Missing for 10: an enumeration of the tool and integration permission keys, explicit allow or deny of external integrations or MCP servers, team-wide or admin enforcement (individual users can bypass prompts with --dangerously-skip-permissions), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can control which external tools and integrations the agent is allowed to access

citations.quote: Each permission key maps to an action ("allow", "ask", or "deny"), or a pattern object for fine-grained control.
Control which actions require your approval before Slate proceeds.
